exposure: mode of birth (vaginal delivery vs. cesarean section)
presence of Ankylosing Spondylitis (AS vs. control group)
outcome: sacroiliac joint (SIJ) shape (specifically enlargement of anterior, superior, and middle regions)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 36 women with Ankylosing Spondylitis and 34 women in a healthy control group, whose pelvis X-ray images were analyzed.
finding: Vaginal delivery is associated with increased sacroiliac joint (SIJ) enlargement in both healthy individuals and those with ankylosing spondylitis (AS).
mod_finding: Delivery type independently influences SIJ morphology, and cesarean section (C/S) may serve as a protective procedure for preserving SIJ shape, especially in AS patients.
